{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. {"notes":"Study findings huge: brass seal press = likely weapon (blood, nick, blue wax matching Edmund's cuff), and North Quay Services owned by Miles with £2,400 estate payments — likely where pension money went. Miles claims he was in study all evening, asked Edmund to postpone accounts (my private knowledge). Strong financial motive + opportunity. Route findings to inspector first. Hear Iris out privately; her scarf could be a plant. Withhold scarf detail publicly to avoid falsely pinning Iris.","actions":[{"type":"accept","chat":"iris-nell"},{"type":"share","chat":"nell-inspector","evidence":"study-company"},{"type":"share","chat":"nell-inspector","evidence":"study-press"},{"type":"say","chat":"nell-inspector","text":"Inspector — I searched the study. The heavy brass seal press has a fresh nick, dried blood and blue wax in the die, and it's been wiped. That blue wax matches the smear on Edmund's cuff. And the filing cabinet holds papers: North Quay Services, sole owner Miles Trent, with £2,400 of estate money paid to it. That may be where the stopped pension money went. One more thing you should weigh carefully: at 19:35 I saw Miles ask Edmund to postpone the accounts review, and Edmund refused."},{"type":"say","chat":"nell-inspector","text":"I must be honest and cautious about one more sighting. At about 19:48 I saw a person in a green scarf carry a dark folder into the library. I could NOT see the face. Iris often wears such a scarf, but it hangs in the hall and anyone could have taken it. Please don't treat this as proof against Iris — it isn't."},{"type":"share","chat":"nell-inspector","evidence":"nell-sighting"},{"type":"say","chat":"iris-nell","text":"I'll listen, Iris. What did you want to say?"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"To help the timeline: I was about the ground floor and the hall after dinner. Around 19:48 I saw someone go into the library carrying a dark folder — but I honestly could not see their face, so I won't name anyone. Miles, you say you were in the study the whole while — did you hear or see anyone pass toward the library?"}]}
